checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add per-note waveform (instrument) overrides

impact_assessment.why: Waveform is score-wide, so voices in a chord or counter-melody cannot have different timbres.
impact_assessment.benefits: An inst directive lets one note switch oscillator while the rest of the phrase keeps its voice; MIDI and WAV stay deterministic.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: WAV and MIDI golden vectors must not change when no override is used; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: the running wave must reset predictably with inst default, and generated notes must inherit the chosen --wave.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Give Note a concrete Wave field, update score and generator constructors together, add byte-comparison and parse tests, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 61 tests green; per-note oscillator overrides verified with byte comparisons and generated-note inheritance; golden vectors unchanged
Task 'coda-note-wave' completed successfully.
checkpoints.head: c9736327476392f089e0d633e6fe9dc612817606

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add a deterministic score linter command

impact_assessment.why: Parse errors are caught, but questionable yet legal scores (extreme pitch, silent notes, clipping risk) produce audio with no feedback.
impact_assessment.benefits: coda lint gives inspectable, deterministic warnings before rendering, so a bad score can be caught without listening.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: lint must never change WAV/MIDI bytes or exit non-zero for warnings; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: warnings must be generated in a stable order.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a pure lint module with exact-output tests, route a new lint command before rendering, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 65 tests green; lint output pinned byte-for-byte in a CLI test; WAV/MIDI output unchanged
Task 'coda-lint' completed successfully.
checkpoints.head: f79394cbfe46c2b205e07d560766ae9cd1f8e750

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add named ADSR envelope presets

impact_assessment.why: Writing four envelope numbers for every voice is tedious; common shapes deserve a name.
impact_assessment.benefits: pluck/pad/organ/stab/bow presets make scores readable and let one score mix articulation styles without four numbers per note.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: WAV/MIDI golden vectors must not change when no preset is used; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: preset default must restore the score envelope exactly.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add Envelope::preset with unit tests, wire a running preset directive into the parser alongside env, add byte-comparison tests, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 68 tests green; presets are byte-equivalent to their explicit ADSR numbers and reset correctly
Task 'coda-env-presets' completed successfully.
checkpoints.head: a17503c61308c70d94e754a9867d1150c1e195de

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add canonical score serialization with round-trip tests

impact_assessment.why: Generative pieces can be rendered but not saved as editable scores; a canonical serializer closes that loop.
impact_assessment.benefits: Any Score (including seeded arrangements) can be written back as source that parses to the identical Score, using the existing parser for deserialization.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: WAV/MIDI bytes and golden vectors must not change; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: every per-note override must survive the round-trip.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a pure serialize function with an exact golden string and round-trip tests over all generative styles, route .coda output explicitly, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 72 tests green; parse(serialize(score)) equals score for all styles, and a cursor bug in at/note placement was found and fixed by the round-trip test
Task 'coda-score-roundtrip' completed successfully.
checkpoints.head: 8bfe8087bad1c82280f5cbeb072fbcad647c34e5

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add deterministic score transposition

impact_assessment.why: Changing key currently means hand-editing every pitch; a transpose operation makes the compiler useful for arrangement.
impact_assessment.benefits: A single --semitones option shifts every pitched note while preserving timing, velocity, pan and envelopes; round-trip by inverse transpose is byte-identical.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: rests and non-pitch fields must be untouched and golden vectors unchanged when the option is absent; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a pure transpose module with note-level tests, apply it at one point after composition, add inverse-transpose byte-equivalence tests, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 78 tests green; inverse transposition restores byte-identical audio and CLI semitone routing verified
Task 'coda-transpose' completed successfully.
checkpoints.head: e17b2deba953a811260c7bb305f2a422f45c375e

checkpoints.description: [1/1] Restore --wave override for parsed scores

impact_assessment.why: After notes gained their own wave field, --wave only changed the score default, so render from a file ignored it.
impact_assessment.benefits: The documented --wave override works again for render, digest and export-score, not just seed.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: seed behavior already correct and must stay; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Propagate the override to every note as well as the score default, add a byte-level regression test, and rerun all gates.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 79 tests green; --wave override now reaches parsed notes and is pinned by a byte-level CLI test
Task 'coda-wave-override-fix' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add seeded score variation

impact_assessment.why: A single score can only be heard one way; a deterministic variation command turns it into a family of related pieces without manual editing.
impact_assessment.benefits: vary applies bounded, seeded changes to pitch, velocity, pan and timbre; amount 0 is an exact identity; the result is an ordinary editable score.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: amount 0 must return a byte-identical Score and all varied fields must stay in valid ranges; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a pure vary module with identity/determinism/bounds tests, a CLI command routing to canonical .coda output, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 85 tests green; seeded variation is byte-identical for equal seeds, identity at amount 0, and output re-parses cleanly
